gloss: awareness / awakening; conscious light (= prakāśa); the title-term and central category of the poem
the supreme non-dual Śiva, 'sustainer of the world' (jagad-bharaṇa); the deity and metaphysical absolute of the poem
the Supreme Lord, intrinsic Self of all beings; the absolute, not a generic 'God'
intrinsic nature / own-being; Bhairava as the essence of all existents
power; the Lord's inseparable creative energy, also the personified Supreme Goddess
the Supreme Goddess, the Lord's own power, who tastes her own nature in the play of manifestation
absolute autonomy / sovereign freedom; the defining attribute of consciousness in Pratyabhijñā
the Unsurpassed / supreme; Abhinavagupta's name for the absolute, identified with the power to accomplish the impossible
the power to accomplish the utterly impossible; the signature Pratyabhijñā definition of divine freedom
reflection of the universe in consciousness, as in a mirror; the reflection-theory of manifestation
perfect fullness, neither diminished nor increased; attribute of the Goddess and of liberation
the inert / insentient, marked by partitioned, delimited light; the contrast to awareness (bodha)
creation and dissolution, effected simultaneously (yugapad) in the Lord's play, not sequential cosmology
transmigration; here redefined as the non-recognition (aparijñāna) of the Self
full recognition (Pratyabhijñā = 're-cognition'); its absence (aparijñāna) is bondage, its presence is liberation
liberation, the full recognition of the reality (tattva), granted from the Supreme Lord
liberation while still embodied; the fullness of the awakened, not a post-mortem escape
non-difference: of power and its holder (v.3), and of bondage and release (v.14)
the powers of will, [limited] action (kalā = kriyā/limitation), and knowledge; the trident (śūla) of three śaktis on which Bhairava rests
